style.vernacular: Arctic Danish-influenced capital on bare rock: small timber-clad houses painted in saturated red, yellow, blue and green with white window frames and low-pitched dark metal roofs; long four-to-five-storey concrete apartment blocks from the 1960s-70s (Blok P era) in muted yellow, ochre or grey; modern public buildings in timber, copper and glass; the historic colonial harbour has red and ochre timber warehouses. Little vegetation: lichen, dwarf birch and bare gneiss. Colours are estimates from general knowledge unless a building entry says sourced.
style.ornament: Horizontal or vertical timber cladding in strong primary colours with white-framed windows; wooden church towers with clocks; copper cladding on new public buildings; apartment blocks with coloured panel bands; Greenlandic and Danish flags; stone-and-gravel terrain around buildings.

sources.what: Church of Our Saviour is a timber building clad in red panels with a wooden tower added 1928: confirms the red-timber colonial vernacular
recent public buildings use copper-clad angular blocks inspired by ice floes (C. F. Moller, 2011)
